gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-cardo: Plain-spoken and sturdy, Bellota Text draws its bars as heavy as its stems. Cardo follows with a text serif whose thin strokes stay sturdy, a literary voice beside it.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-kulim-park: Friendly and confident, Bellota Text opens its curves wide with no calligraphic shading, and Kulim Park backs it with a sans-serif of generous gaps. Their strongest trait is shared openness.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-sour-gummy: Sour Gummy reads modern and crisp, with wide gaps that hold up small. Under Bellota Text, with its marker-drawn plainness and commanding presence, a long page would feel steady and unhurried.
gen-gf-bellota-text-gf-spectral: Bellota Text has a wire-like line, thin and open with no shading. Its commanding look suits headings, while Spectral, a text serif with a thick-thin difference and stems a touch heavier than crossbars, handles the bookish reading.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-cabin: Bruno Ace draws a ruler-straight line of constant width, one character per beat. Cabin follows warmly, its bent-tubing letters and open terminals making a longer plain sans read comfortably.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-fs-rowan: Bruno Ace is drawn with a ruler, one constant width and no hairlines anywhere. It handles the expressive display work, while Rowan, a classic serif with generous curves and sturdy hairlines, carries the friendly literary reading.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-actor: Bruno Ace lingers, one character per beat, as a thread of ink. Its strongest quality is the distinctive display line against Actor, a clean modern sans-serif with wide s curves.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-cardo: Expressive and ruler-straight, Bruno Ace sets crossbars level with its stems, while Cardo, a text serif, shows only faint modulation up close. Each keeps its own voice.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-carme: Carme is modern and neutral, its line like spaghetti laid out in letters. Bruno Ace delivers the distinctive, lingering display rhythm, while Carme does the quieter work of open counters leading outward.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-chakra-petch: Distinctive and unmistakable, Bruno Ace holds a constant ruler-drawn line across its headings. Chakra Petch, a contemporary sans-serif with cupped round letters, does the steadier reading work.
